lessonActivities.title: Tense Backshift Rules ⏪
lessonActivities.content:
Now let's level up! 🎯 When the reporting verb is in the past, most tenses shift 'back' one step. Tense backshift helps you report past conversations accurately.

Formation: [Subject] + [reporting verb in past] + (that) + [backshifted clause]. Example: 'I am tired' → He said he was tired.

Direct TenseReported TenseExampleKey Signal
Present Simple→ Past Simple'I like coffee' → She said she liked coffeeGeneral facts, habits
Present Continuous→ Past Continuous'I'm working' → He said he was workingActions in progress
Present Perfect→ Past Perfect'I have finished' → She said she had finishedCompleted actions with present relevance
Will→ Would'I'll call you' → She said she would call meFuture promises/plans
Can→ Could'I can swim' → He said he could swimAbility/possibility

Fun fact: Past Perfect and modal verbs (might/could/would/should) don't change! 🎉

Memory trick: Think of a timeline: Direct speech is 'now', reported speech moves everything one step into the 'past'.
examples: Positive: 'I have finished' → She said she had finished.
Negative: 'I don't know' → He said he didn't know.
Question form: 'Do you understand?' → She asked if I understood.
functions: Reporting past conversations with correct tense shifts
lessonActivities.tips: Memory trick: Think of a timeline: Direct speech is 'now', reported speech moves everything one step into the 'past'.

lessonActivities.title: Modal Verbs in Reported Speech: What Changes? 🔑
lessonActivities.content:
Here's a crucial rule! 🔑 When you report speech with modal verbs, some change and some don't! This trips up many learners.

The Rule: After a past reporting verb, will→would, can→could, may→might, must→had to. But might/could/would/should/ought to stay the same! Example: 'I must go' → He said he had to go.

Modal in DirectMeaningReported FormExample
willfuture intentionwould'I'll help' → She said she would help.
canability/permissioncould'I can swim' → He said he could swim.
maypossibility/permissionmight'It may rain' → She said it might rain.
mustobligationhad to'I must study' → He said he had to study.
shouldadvice (NO CHANGE)should'You should rest' → She said I should rest.

Fun fact: 'Must' for logical deduction ('He must be tired') often stays 'must' in reported speech! 🤔

Never forget: Modals of deduction (must/can't) and advice (should) often don't change. Modals of future/ability/permission usually do!
examples: With 'will': 'I will call' → She said she would call.
With 'can': 'I can help' → He said he could help.
With 'must': 'I must leave' → She said she had to leave.
No change: 'You should try' → He said I should try.
functions: Identifying which modals change in reported speech
lessonActivities.tips: Never forget: Modals of deduction (must/can't) and advice (should) often don't change. Modals of future/ability/permission usually do!

writingActivities.question: Report these statements with correct tense backshift: 'I like pizza' and 'She is studying now'.
writingActivities.hint: Present Simple → Past Simple; Present Continuous → Past Continuous. Example: He said he liked pizza.

gameActivities.hint: 'Can' changes to 'could' in reported speech when the reporting verb is past.
